key_insight: WOVEN shows that multimodal LLM failures on spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning can be traced to a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning, which can be learned as a reusable foundation across tasks.
engineering_relevance: For multimodal systems, the paper offers a practical training recipe to improve visual world modeling with modest, transferable supervision instead of task-specific data alone.
method: Built WOVEN, a 36,076-example dataset organized by scene, action, and reasoning type from realistic rollouts of video-pretrained generative models.
Evaluated 38 frontier MLLMs to isolate systematic visual transition reasoning deficits across model families and scale.
Trained models at multiple scales and compared which supervision types transfer best to external benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on 22 of 26 external benchmarks, up to 27.3 percentage points, and that WOVEN can replace 30–50% of task-specific training data with similar accuracy.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality and realism of generated rollouts, so transfer may weaken if the visual state changes or downstream domains differ substantially from WOVEN.
paper_title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
